title: Shipments from each stock line
prompt: Warehouse managers want each stock line next to the shipments that draw on it. Write `solve(inventory, shipments)` so it returns `warehouse_id`, `sku`, `sku_name`, `on_hand`, `shipment_id` and `quantity`.
rules: A stock line is one warehouse and one SKU. A shipment draws on the line with the same `warehouse_id` and the same `sku`.
A stock line appears once per shipment that draws on it. A stock line with no shipments appears once, with `shipment_id` and `quantity` missing.
Shipments with no matching stock line are not listed. Return only these six columns, in this order.
hints: The same SKU is stocked in several warehouses, so matching on `sku` alone would pair a shipment with every warehouse's stock.
Pass both key columns as a list: `on=["warehouse_id", "sku"]`. A row pairs only when both are equal.
Every stock line must appear, so `inventory` is the left side of a left join.
explanation: The key of a stock line is two columns, so join on both: `inventory.join(shipments, on=["warehouse_id", "sku"], how="left")`, then select the six columns. A left join from `inventory` keeps lines with no shipments, with NULL shipment columns. Joining on `sku` alone would pair each tape shipment with the tape stock of every warehouse, and the key columns would be ambiguous; joining on `warehouse_id` alone pairs it with every SKU in its warehouse.
